page: Microsoft Azure M128-32ms is a memory-intensive virtual machine from the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8280L processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 105 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX, AVX-512F, and AES instructions. This server is equipped with an exceptionally large memory capacity of 3892.0 GB, yielding 121.62 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 4194 GB SSD, and the instance is premium storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear tradeoff between single-core compute and memory capabilities. Single-core CPU performance, measured by stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 10%, and single-threaded compression tasks are similarly limited. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth are more robust. Large-block memory write bandwidth is strong, placing in the top 25% of tested servers, while read bandwidth and multi-core Geekbench scores remain in the average tier.

Given its massive memory-to-vCPU ratio, this server offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads rather than compute-heavy processing. It is designed for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise relational databases, and heavy caching layers like Redis, where average multi-core throughput and high memory density are required.
